description: The audio system used on Simpledeav case study 03 (Airbnb). Use it unchanged for every new documentary episode. It is tuned for a single deep male narrator, one licensed cinematic bed, and restrained Foley.

referenceEpisode.title: The Startup That Sold Cereal to Survive

voice.voiceCharacter: mature male, deep, warm, neutral international English, documentary not trailer
voice.pausePolicy: Generate one segment per story act, then cap any internal silence longer than 0.30s at 0.30s and trim segment edges to 0.05s. This keeps ~170 wpm without an audibly rushed read. Never time-stretch after generation.
voice.segmentation: One TTS call per act, placed back-to-back on a continuous timeline. Act cuts sit ~0.2s before each sentence start; do not insert dramatic gaps just to match a storyboard.

wordBudget.note: If the script is longer, raise the rate before cutting words. Keep the approved script verbatim.

subtitles.source: Edge word boundaries only; never invented
subtitles.splitOn: sentence punctuation, then commas after 5 words
subtitles.render: Two lines max, 46 characters per line target, no background box beyond a soft scrim.

music.style: modern documentary: emotional piano, warm pads, restrained percussion, one build, resolved ending

sourcePreparation.note: The 2.6kHz dip carves intelligibility space for the voice. Normalise the bed once, never per-scene.

mix.points: Animate 0.10 at the open, 0.145-0.16 through the setup, 0.185-0.225 through the growth, 0.15-0.17 for the resolution, 0 at the final frame.
mix.measuredResult: about -32 LUFS under narration, -28 LUFS in gaps; 16dB below the voice

sfx.rule: One intentional sound per story beat. Never stack two impacts within 0.12s. No risers under dialogue unless they peak in a gap.

palette.asset: original synthesized sting + Mixkit low impact

originalFoley.rule: Synthesize object-specific Foley locally when no licensed sample exists. Never use a generic whoosh for a physical object.

mix.note: Remotion sums without a master limiter. Keep narration at 0.92, Foley at the fixed 0.62 gain, and music at or below 0.25 linear so the sum stays under 0 dBFS.

qualityGates: narration file matches the composition duration within 0.25s
last subtitle cue ends before the brand reveal
music bed covers the full film and automation ends at 0
every SFX file exists, sits inside the timeline, and no two impacts stack
every audio asset has a recorded licence
